A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FCaps/CLSP research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison despite repagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation-quality evaluations, retrieval and classification experiments, human-rating correlations, and training ablations in Tables 2–5 and 8–10.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the human evaluation and appendix ablations. Retention from v1 does not change their status as original results.

M1.justification: The captioning and verification pipeline, SPEAR-XLarge/RoBERTa dual encoder, two-stage contrastive objectives, and task scheduler remain unchanged. Revised wording and the replacement captioner citation do not establish a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain FCaps-Emilia and FCaps-PSCBase, ParaSpeechCaps retrieval and human-alignment evaluations, and IEMOCAP/RAVDESS/CREMA-D classification. Newly discussed datasets such as NLSpeech and LibriTTS-R appear in related work, not new experiments.

E2.justification: The cascaded annotation comparator remains unchanged. Tables 3 and 5 retain LAION-AI CLAP, GLAP, and ParaCLAP; Table 4 additionally retains the same Auden-Voice CLAP results attributed to prior work. New discussion citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The reported protocols remain the same: 1,000 clips for annotation evaluation, 241 for retrieval, identical classification settings and metrics, and 20 raters with 30 clips per trait category. Training still uses 1.2M first-stage steps and 4k second-stage steps. The judge identifier remains gemini-3-pro-preview.

E4.justification: Appendices B/C retain the same prompting and multi-positive caption case studies, and Appendix G retains the same training-stage, loss-weight, and scheduler ablations. Removing the main-text Section 5.2.5 summary does not remove these analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report five judge runs with randomized caption ordering, the same uncertainty reporting in Table 2, and the same p < 0.01 significance statement in Table 5. No new repeated-run or statistical estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Figure 1 changes the five example scores from 34.5, 18.6, 38.4, 14.1, and 40.4 to 0.62, 0.33, 0.68, 0.24, and 0.72, preserving the captions and ranking. The numerical conversion is unexplained, so this does not establish a performance gain. Main benchmark and appendix ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same contrastive losses, target distributions, and scheduling rule. The caption-taxonomy rewrite restates existing distinctions without adding mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: FCaps, its end-to-end annotation pipeline, multi-granular CLSP representations, and strong task performance and human alignment. The resource-release announcement changes availability information rather than these core claims.

C2.justification: A new discussion in Section 5.2.4 explicitly proposes CLSP for instruction-following TTS evaluation, large-scale benchmarking, and speech-data filtering, emphasizing practicality relative to LLM judges. These are additional applicability interpretations without corresponding new experiments. The English-only and limited-style-coverage limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 only promises public resources; v3 reports public code, dataset, and model availability, supplies repository and dataset/model access locations, and specifies CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for FCaps and Apache 2.0 for CLSP. This substantially expands access and reuse information. Existing implementation settings remain intact, although the judge's November 2025 date qualifier is removed.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 substantially expands the generic cascaded-pipeline summary into dataset-specific accounts of human annotation, templates, and LLM rewriting. The new discussion also positions CLSP within TTS and speech-quality evaluation literature. Table 1 changes DreamVoiceDB's Free-Text designation from no to yes, and the captioner attribution replaces Omni-captioner with the Qwen3-Omni technical report.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify caption terminology and condense model, judge, and implementation descriptions. v3 expands related work, adds an application discussion and acknowledgments, and removes the standalone main-text ablation summary while retaining Appendix G. The overall organization and most prose remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 1 reorders the LibriTTS-P and DreamVoiceDB rows, Figure 3 moves between columns, and Figure 4 moves to the following page. Text and appendix placement reflow, and printed page numbers disappear. The existing figure/table collection and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves practical documentation by replacing promised resource release with concrete access and licensing information, and provides a more explicit account of earlier annotation methods. These benefits improve usability and research context while the scientific method and experimental support remain stable. The gains are limited by unexplained Figure 1 score changes and newly suggested TTS/filtering applications that receive no additional validation.
